input.command:
gh pr create --title "perf(graph,vcs): bound git revwalk, cache tag globs, fix inference pathspecs" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- Bound `commits_since_with_pathspec`'s revwalk to `since..HEAD` using gix's `with_hidden` frontier algorithm instead of two full unbounded walks — measured ~265x speedup (105.2ms → 0.397ms avg at 3000 commits), preserves the existing branchy-history correctness invariant.
- Cache compiled tag-template glob matchers across packages in `TagIndex::build`, avoiding redundant recompile+rescan when multiple packages share a `[[package-set]]` template.
- Fix commit-inference pathspecs to scope to the package's source directory instead of its manifest file path, so the `inference` feature actually matches real source changes.

Each finding is its own commit with a dedicated regression test confirmed failing before the fix, and passed an independent read-only review agent. Full detail (including measured before/after numbers) in `.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md`'s Track 7 entry.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p callisto-vcs -p callisto-graph` — 559/559 passed
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] Two independent review agents (explicitly read-only) passed all three findings, including a deep branchy-history correctness trace on the revwalk change
- [ ] Full-workspace `just ci` not run this session — see note below

**Note**: a pre-existing, unrelated environment issue was found and diagnosed during this work (`cargo nextest` + global `commit.gpgsign=true` causes ~120s hangs across ~66 git-fixture test call sites in 16 files, root-caused and reproduced on a clean checkout independent of this branch). It's documented in `ACTIVE.md` and deferred to its own track rather than folded into this PR's scope.

https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)"

A prior session diagnosed a real bug: `cargo nextest` spawns each test binary with no controlling TTY. On a developer machine with `git config --global commit.gpgsign true` set, any test that creates a real on-disk git repo and calls `git commit` without locally disabling signing triggers a real GPG signing attempt that `pinentry` can't service (no TTY to prompt on) — the test hangs ~120-140s waiting on a gpg-agent/pinentry timeout, or fails outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". This affects ~66 `git commit` call sites across 16 files in the workspace's test suite. There's a shared, canonical fixture helper — `callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo` — used by 2 of those files; the other ~14 independently duplicate their own version.

## The fix (this review's scope — only `crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`)

`init_repo` now runs 5 `git` commands instead of 3:
```rust
pub fn init_repo(root: &Path) {
    run_git(root, &["init", "-q", "-b", "main"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "user.email", "test@example.com"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "user.name", "Test"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "commit.gpgsign", "false"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "tag.gpgsign", "false"]);
}
```

git add crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(fixtures): make init_repo hermetic against ambient git config

Diagnosed this session: cargo nextest spawns each test binary with no
controlling TTY. On a machine with commit.gpgsign=true set globally,
any test creating a real repo via this shared helper would trigger a
real GPG signing attempt on commit -- pinentry can't prompt without a
TTY, so the test hangs ~120-140s on a gpg-agent timeout, or fails
outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". init_repo now sets
commit.gpgsign=false/tag.gpgsign=false in the repo's local config
(never touching the developer's real ~/.gitconfig), which git respects
as taking precedence over any global config. Also pins the initial
branch name (-b main), since init.defaultBranch is similarly ambient.

Regression test writes a throwaway GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL override (not the
real global config) forcing commit.gpgsign=true and an unusable
gpg.program, then asserts a commit still succeeds -- confirmed failing
before this fix, confirmed passing after. Fast and deterministic (the
poisoned gpg.program path doesn't exist, so a poisoned commit fails
immediately via "cannot exec" rather than actually hanging).

This is the canonical fixture helper (callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo);
~14 other independently-duplicated init_repo/run_git helpers across the
workspace still need the same fix -- follow-up commits, not covered here.
EOF
)"

Reference the canonical fix commit `a4eb5f0` plus your new commits. Commit that as its own final `docs:` commit.
8. Do NOT push or open a PR — leave that for the coordinating session.

Report back: which files you actually touched vs skipped (and why, if any), all commit SHAs, and confirmation that `cargo test --workspace` (or per-crate equivalents if workspace-wide is too slow given known nextest slowness elsewhere) is green for every crate you touched.

+Lighter TDD loop tier (no formal spec/plan, one crate per commit). Fixes a real bug surfaced during
+Track 7 (`track-7-revwalk-bounding`, PR #13, not yet merged when this track was cut): `cargo nextest`
+spawns each test binary with no controlling TTY, and on a developer machine with
+`commit.gpgsign=true`/`tag.gpgsign=true` set globally, any test that creates a real on-disk git repo
+and calls `git commit`/`git tag` without locally disabling signing triggers a real GPG signing attempt
+that `pinentry` can't service (no TTY to prompt on) — the test hangs ~120-140s waiting on a
+gpg-agent/pinentry timeout, or fails outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". Diagnosed via
+direct reproduction (confirmed NOT gpg-agent lock contention: 8 fully concurrent `git commit`s outside
+nextest completed in ~1s; confirmed the specific `cargo test` vs `cargo nextest` TTY distinction is the
+actual trigger) — see `feedback_diagnose_dont_guess_environment_issues.md` in the memory index for the
+process this followed. Two audit agents mapped the full scope: ~66 real `git commit` call sites across
+16 files build real git fixture repos without a local `commit.gpgsign=false` guard; a canonical shared
+helper existed (`callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo`) but only 2 of ~14 independently-duplicated
+`init_repo`/`run_git`-style helpers actually used it; a parallel audit confirmed no equivalent gap
+exists for npm/pip/cargo/twine/maturin shell-outs (all go through a mockable `CommandRunner` trait in
+both production and test code).
+
+**Fix**: `callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo` (the canonical helper) now sets `commit.gpgsign=false`/
+`tag.gpgsign=false` via local `git config` calls (never touching the developer's real `~/.gitconfig`,
+which git respects as taking lower precedence than local config) and pins `-b main` on `git init`
+(`init.defaultBranch` is a related ambient-config gap). A regression test
+(`crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`) proves this hermetically and fast: it writes a throwaway
+`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-pointed poisoned config file (not the real global config) forcing
+`commit.gpgsign=true` and an unusable `gpg.program`, then asserts a commit still succeeds — confirmed
+failing before the fix, passing after, and independently re-verified by the reviewing agent via its own
+standalone experiment (0.05s run time, no hang, since the poisoned `gpg.program` path doesn't exist so
+a poisoned attempt fails immediately via "cannot exec" rather than actually invoking pinentry).
+
+Every other independently-duplicated helper across the workspace got the identical two-line fix
+(hand-patched in place, not migrated to import the shared helper — `callisto-fixtures` is
+AGPL-3.0-only, and per this project's layer-isolation invariant no new dev-dependency edges on it were
+introduced):

+  test's own inline init sequence (didn't call `init_repo` at all); `src/access.rs`'s `init_repo` fn.
+  Verified: `cargo nextest run -p callisto-vcs` — entire 38-test suite now completes in 0.345s (some of
+  these tests previously took 57-84s each under nextest).
+- **callisto-cli** (`f4a55cd7`): `tests/common/mod.rs`'s `setup_polyglot_git_repo`,
+  `tests/strict_flag_tests.rs`'s `make_git_workspace`, `tests/dry_run_invariant_tests.rs`'s `setup_repo`,
+  `src/commands/version.rs`'s `git_init_with_commit` (behind the `inference` feature). Verified:
+  `cargo nextest run -p callisto-cli --test strict_flag_tests --test dry_run_invariant_tests` — 20/20
+  pass in 1.003s total; `dry_run_invariant_tests` is the exact file that originally failed outright
+  with "No pinentry" in the session's first observed failure.
+- **callisto-graph** (`9fb0384e`): `src/commands/snapshot.rs`'s `git_init_with_commit`,
+  `src/commands/version.rs`'s `git_init_with_commit`, `tests/version_tests.rs`, `tests/snapshot_tests.rs`'s
+  `init_git_repo_with_commit`, `tests/publish_tests.rs`. `tests/tag_sha_fabrication_test.rs` already had
+  the correct fix (with its own explanatory comment) — left untouched; it's the file this fix pattern
+  was modeled on. Verified: `cargo nextest run -p callisto-graph --test snapshot_tests --test
+  version_tests --test publish_tests` — 38/38 pass in 0.541s total (previously ~60-84s each).
+- **callisto-moon** (`26d14b1b`): `tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs`'s async `run_git`-based init sequences
+  (two duplicate blocks). Verified via `cargo check`/`cargo clippy --features pdk` only (clean) — full
+  execution of this file's real wasmtime-backed sandbox test was not run given the prohibitive combined
+  build cost (native wasmtime/aws-lc-sys compile plus a from-scratch `wasm32-wasip1` build with no
+  cached artifact available); the change is mechanically identical to the four already-fully-verified
+  fixes above. Recommend confirming with a real `just wasm-check`/full test run in CI.

content.text: Confirmed root cause: `Path::new("Cargo.toml").starts_with(".")` is `false` in Rust — `package_paths`'s root-package sentinel `"."` (which real git's own pathspec engine understands as "match everything," and which correctly worked in `package_paths`'s original consumer that shells out to real git) doesn't have that meaning to this codebase's own Rust-based `location_matches` matcher. My Track 7 finding-3 fix newly routes a `"."` pathspec into that matcher for any root-level package, which now matches **zero** commits — worse than the bug it fixed. My test only covered a nested package, missing this edge case. Switching to the Track 7 branch to fix it properly.

But the *new* consumer this session's aggregate.rs fix routes pathspecs into — `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`'s `commits_since_with_pathspec` → `commit_touches_pathspecs` → `location_matches` — is this codebase's own simplified, hand-rolled Rust pathspec matcher, NOT real git. `location_matches` used `changed_path.starts_with(spec)` (`std::path::Path::starts_with`), and **`Path::new("Cargo.toml").starts_with(".")` is `false` in Rust** (confirmed directly: `Path::starts_with` requires whole-component matches, and git diff paths never carry a literal leading `.` component). ```rust
fn location_matches(location: &gix::bstr::BStr, pathspecs: &[PathBuf]) -> bool {

    let changed_path = Path::new(path_str.as_ref());
    pathspecs
        .iter()

**Finding 3 — commit-inference pathspec bug.** `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`'s pathspecs
for commit-based severity inference were built from `pkg.manifests.iter().map(|m| m.path.clone())` —
the manifest *file* path (e.g. `crates/foo/Cargo.toml`) — instead of the package's source
*directory*, so commit-based inference only ever matched commits touching the manifest file itself,
never real source changes, making the `inference` feature (behind a Cargo feature flag) a near-total
no-op for its purpose. Fixed by reusing `crate::changed::package_paths(pkg)` — an existing,
already-tested directory-scoping helper `changed_since_last_tag` already relied on for the identical
purpose. New regression test asserts `aggregate()` hands a recording `SeverityInference` the package
directory (`crates/pkg-a`), not the manifest file path — confirmed failing against the pre-fix code.
Independent review PASS. Commit: `d3a5c434`.

outright with "No pinentry") instead of running in milliseconds. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated

**Post-PR fix — finding 3 exposed a latent bug in `location_matches`.** Real CI on PR #13
(`cargo test --all-features`, enabling the `inference` feature) caught what the scoped local
verification above missed: `changed::package_paths` emits `"."` as the pathspec for a manifest at
the workspace/package root (a single-package repo's `Cargo.toml`) — the same sentinel real git's own
pathspec engine understands as "match everything," correct for that helper's original consumer
(`changed_since_last_tag`, which shells out to real `git`). Finding 3 newly routes that `"."`
pathspec into this codebase's own hand-rolled Rust matcher instead
(`callisto-vcs`'s `commits_since_with_pathspec` → `location_matches`, using `Path::starts_with`) —
and `Path::new("Cargo.toml").starts_with(".")` is `false` in Rust, so a `"."` pathspec silently
matched **zero** commits instead of every commit: a more severe regression than finding 3 itself
fixed, specifically for single-package repos. Fixed in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`'s
`location_matches` by short-circuiting to a match whenever the pathspec itself is exactly `"."`,
mirroring real git's semantics; `ShellGit`'s shelled-out backend was never affected (delegates
matching to the real `git` binary). Regression test on a real repo confirmed failing (empty result)
before the fix. Independent review PASS (confirmed no overreach on non-`.` pathspecs, traced `"."`'s
only producer, confirmed the sibling `ShellGit` path is immune by construction). Commit: `8140b3d`.

200	### Track 7: Git Revwalk Bounding & Redundant I/O — DONE
201	
202	Lighter TDD loop tier (no formal spec/plan, one finding per commit, matching Track 9 / Track
203	6-mechanical's precedent). Three independent findings, all re-verified live in code before fixing.
204	
205	**Finding 1 — unbounded double revwalk.** `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`'s
206	`commits_since_with_pathspec` did two full, unbounded `gix` revwalks every call regardless of how
207	close `since` was to HEAD: one from HEAD, one from `since` collected into a `HashSet` exclusion set
208	— walking the entire repository history on every call. Fixed by replacing both walks with gix's own
209	bounded-walk primitive: `rev_walk(head).with_hidden(since).all()`, which computes a
210	generation-number frontier between the visible (HEAD) and hidden (`since`) tips in one combined walk
211	and never enqueues a parent once it's known to lie only in hidden-only ancestry — the same "boundary
212	commit" algorithm `git rev-list branch ^tag` uses internally, so it structurally preserves the
213	branchy-history correctness the old two-walk approach needed a manual `continue`-not-`break`
214	exclusion set for (verified: the existing `test_commits_since_with_pathspec_includes_pre_tag_branch_commits`
215	regression test, which encodes exactly that scenario, still passes). Measured before/after on a
216	3000-commit linear history with `since=HEAD~5`: old implementation avg 105.2ms/call, new avg
217	0.397ms/call (~265x). A dedicated regression test (`crates/callisto-vcs/tests/revwalk_bound_count_test.rs`,
218	`#[serial]`, process-global visit counter isolated in its own integration binary the same way
219	`tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs` isolates `callisto-manifests`' counters) proves the walk
220	visits exactly the 3 commits between `since` and HEAD on a 33-commit fixture (30 before, 3 after),
221	not the full history — confirmed failing (33 visits) against the old two-walk logic before the fix.
222	Independent review (general-purpose agent, explicitly read-only) additionally hand-traced gix's
223	`compute_hidden_frontier` algorithm in `gix-traverse-0.60.0` against adversarial branch topologies
224	(multiple divergent branches, a branch merging back in after `since`) and confirmed the correctness
225	argument generalizes structurally, not just on the one existing test's specific commit graph. PASS.
226	Commit: `f0a0b8de`.
227	
228	**Finding 2 — per-package glob-matcher recompile.** `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`'s
229	`matching_tags` compiled a fresh `globset::Glob` and rescanned the full tag list on every call, once
230	per package via `TagIndex::build`'s loop — even when a `[[package-set]]` rule's fixed (non-`{name}`)
231	`tag-template` string applies the identical template to many packages at once (measured ~640ms
232	wasted at 1000 packages / 41k tags in the original audit). Fixed via `select_from_tags_cached`, which
233	caches compile+scan results in `TagIndex::build`'s loop keyed by the template's rendered glob string.
234	Regression tests (`crates/callisto-graph/tests/tag_glob_cache_count_test.rs`, `#[serial]`, isolated
235	the same way as finding 1's counter for the same process-global-counter reason) prove 3 packages
236	sharing one template compile the glob exactly once (not 3 times), and 2 packages with distinct
237	default templates still compile separately (proving the cache keys correctly, doesn't over-collapse).
238	Independent review PASS. Commit: `1700f1f9`.
239	
240	**Finding 3 — commit-inference pathspec bug.** `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`'s pathspecs
241	for commit-based severity inference were built from `pkg.manifests.iter().map(|m| m.path.clone())` —
242	the manifest *file* path (e.g. `crates/foo/Cargo.toml`) — instead of the package's source
243	*directory*, so commit-based inference only ever matched commits touching the manifest file itself,
244	never real source changes, making the `inference` feature (behind a Cargo feature flag) a near-total
245	no-op for its purpose. Fixed by reusing `crate::changed::package_paths(pkg)` — an existing,
246	already-tested directory-scoping helper `changed_since_last_tag` already relied on for the identical
247	purpose. New regression test asserts `aggregate()` hands a recording `SeverityInference` the package
248	directory (`crates/pkg-a`), not the manifest file path — confirmed failing against the pre-fix code.
249	Independent review PASS. Commit: `d3a5c434`.
250	
251	**Post-PR fix — finding 3 exposed a latent bug in `location_matches`.** Real CI on PR #13
252	(`cargo test --all-features`, enabling the `inference` feature) caught what the scoped local
253	verification above missed: `changed::package_paths` emits `"."` as the pathspec for a manifest at
254	the workspace/package root (a single-package repo's `Cargo.toml`) — the same sentinel real git's own
255	pathspec engine understands as "match everything," correct for that helper's original consumer
256	(`changed_since_last_tag`, which shells out to real `git`). Finding 3 newly routes that `"."`
257	pathspec into this codebase's own hand-rolled Rust matcher instead
258	(`callisto-vcs`'s `commits_since_with_pathspec` → `location_matches`, using `Path::starts_with`) —
259	and `Path::new("Cargo.toml").starts_with(".")` is `false` in Rust, so a `"."` pathspec silently
260	matched **zero** commits instead of every commit: a more severe regression than finding 3 itself
261	fixed, specifically for single-package repos. Fixed in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`'s
262	`location_matches` by short-circuiting to a match whenever the pathspec itself is exactly `"."`,
263	mirroring real git's semantics; `ShellGit`'s shelled-out backend was never affected (delegates
264	matching to the real `git` binary). Regression test on a real repo confirmed failing (empty result)
265	before the fix. Independent review PASS (confirmed no overreach on non-`.` pathspecs, traced `"."`'s
266	only producer, confirmed the sibling `ShellGit` path is immune by construction). Commit: `8140b3d`.
267	
268	Every fix's `just ci`-equivalent verification: `cargo nextest run -p callisto-vcs -p callisto-graph`
269	(the real test runner `just ci`'s `test` recipe invokes, scoped to the two touched crates) — 559/559
270	passed, 0 failed, clean. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D
271	warnings` clean throughout. A full-workspace `cargo nextest run --workspace` was not completed this
272	session — see the environment note below; the scoped run above is the load-bearing verification for
273	these three findings' own correctness.
274	
275	**Environment finding surfaced this session, deferred to a new track (not fixed here, user
276	decision):** diagnosed (not guessed — verified via isolated reproduction) that `cargo nextest`
277	spawns each test binary with no controlling TTY, while the operator's machine has
278	`commit.gpgsign=true`/`tag.gpgsign=true` set globally. ~66 real `git commit` call sites across 16
279	files create real on-disk git fixture repos without locally disabling gpg signing (only 2 files guard
280	against it, one via a shared-but-underused `callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo` helper, one via a
281	per-file ad hoc fix that was never propagated) — under nextest's no-TTY child processes, `pinentry`
282	can't prompt, so every such test hangs ~120-140s waiting on a gpg-agent/pinentry timeout (or fails
283	outright with "No pinentry") instead of running in milliseconds. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated
284	to Track 7's changes (reproduces identically on a clean stashed checkout); confirmed NOT a
285	gpg-agent-lock-contention issue (8 fully concurrent `git commit`s outside nextest completed in ~1s).
286	A parallel audit of every other subprocess shell-out in the workspace (npm/pip/cargo/twine/maturin)
287	found no equivalent gap — all real ecosystem-CLI invocations already go through the mockable
288	`CommandRunner` trait in both production and test code; the only other instance of the same git-signing
289	gap is `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs` (guards `tag.gpgSign` but not
290	`commit.gpgsign`, same root cause). User decision: fix as its own new track (harden the one canonical
291	`callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo` to set `commit.gpgsign=false`/`tag.gpgsign=false`/`-b main`
292	locally per-repo, then migrate ~13 duplicated/ad-hoc helpers to call it), not folded into Track 7.
293	Also noted in passing: unnamed `#[serial]` (from `serial_test`) shares one global lock across every
294	test using it in a binary, compounding queueing delays for unrelated fast tests during the slow run —
295	minor, same deferred track can address if convenient.

297	### Track 8: Git Fixture Hermeticity — DONE
298	
299	Lighter TDD loop tier (no formal spec/plan, one crate per commit). Fixes a real bug surfaced during
300	Track 7 (`track-7-revwalk-bounding`, PR #13, not yet merged when this track was cut): `cargo nextest`
301	spawns each test binary with no controlling TTY, and on a developer machine with
302	`commit.gpgsign=true`/`tag.gpgsign=true` set globally, any test that creates a real on-disk git repo
303	and calls `git commit`/`git tag` without locally disabling signing triggers a real GPG signing attempt
304	that `pinentry` can't service (no TTY to prompt on) — the test hangs ~120-140s waiting on a
305	gpg-agent/pinentry timeout, or fails outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". Diagnosed via
306	direct reproduction (confirmed NOT gpg-agent lock contention: 8 fully concurrent `git commit`s outside
307	nextest completed in ~1s; confirmed the specific `cargo test` vs `cargo nextest` TTY distinction is the
308	actual trigger) — see `feedback_diagnose_dont_guess_environment_issues.md` in the memory index for the
309	process this followed. Two audit agents mapped the full scope: ~66 real `git commit` call sites across
310	16 files build real git fixture repos without a local `commit.gpgsign=false` guard; a canonical shared
311	helper existed (`callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo`) but only 2 of ~14 independently-duplicated
312	`init_repo`/`run_git`-style helpers actually used it; a parallel audit confirmed no equivalent gap
313	exists for npm/pip/cargo/twine/maturin shell-outs (all go through a mockable `CommandRunner` trait in
314	both production and test code).
315	
316	**Fix**: `callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo` (the canonical helper) now sets `commit.gpgsign=false`/
317	`tag.gpgsign=false` via local `git config` calls (never touching the developer's real `~/.gitconfig`,
318	which git respects as taking lower precedence than local config) and pins `-b main` on `git init`
319	(`init.defaultBranch` is a related ambient-config gap). A regression test
320	(`crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`) proves this hermetically and fast: it writes a throwaway
321	`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-pointed poisoned config file (not the real global config) forcing
322	`commit.gpgsign=true` and an unusable `gpg.program`, then asserts a commit still succeeds — confirmed
323	failing before the fix, passing after, and independently re-verified by the reviewing agent via its own
324	standalone experiment (0.05s run time, no hang, since the poisoned `gpg.program` path doesn't exist so
325	a poisoned attempt fails immediately via "cannot exec" rather than actually invoking pinentry).
326	
327	Every other independently-duplicated helper across the workspace got the identical two-line fix
328	(hand-patched in place, not migrated to import the shared helper — `callisto-fixtures` is
329	AGPL-3.0-only, and per this project's layer-isolation invariant no new dev-dependency edges on it were

### Track 7: Git Revwalk Bounding & Redundant I/O — DONE

Lighter TDD loop tier (no formal spec/plan, one finding per commit, matching Track 9 / Track
6-mechanical's precedent). Three independent findings, all re-verified live in code before fixing.

**Finding 1 — unbounded double revwalk.** `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`'s
`commits_since_with_pathspec` did two full, unbounded `gix` revwalks every call regardless of how
close `since` was to HEAD: one from HEAD, one from `since` collected into a `HashSet` exclusion set
— walking the entire repository history on every call. Fixed by replacing both walks with gix's own
bounded-walk primitive: `rev_walk(head).with_hidden(since).all()`, which computes a
generation-number frontier between the visible (HEAD) and hidden (`since`) tips in one combined walk
and never enqueues a parent once it's known to lie only in hidden-only ancestry — the same "boundary
commit" algorithm `git rev-list branch ^tag` uses internally, so it structurally preserves the
branchy-history correctness the old two-walk approach needed a manual `continue`-not-`break`
exclusion set for (verified: the existing `test_commits_since_with_pathspec_includes_pre_tag_branch_commits`
regression test, which encodes exactly that scenario, still passes). Measured before/after on a
3000-commit linear history with `since=HEAD~5`: old implementation avg 105.2ms/call, new avg
0.397ms/call (~265x). A dedicated regression test (`crates/callisto-vcs/tests/revwalk_bound_count_test.rs`,
`#[serial]`, process-global visit counter isolated in its own integration binary the same way
`tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs` isolates `callisto-manifests`' counters) proves the walk
visits exactly the 3 commits between `since` and HEAD on a 33-commit fixture (30 before, 3 after),
not the full history — confirmed failing (33 visits) against the old two-walk logic before the fix.
Independent review (general-purpose agent, explicitly read-only) additionally hand-traced gix's
`compute_hidden_frontier` algorithm in `gix-traverse-0.60.0` against adversarial branch topologies
(multiple divergent branches, a branch merging back in after `since`) and confirmed the correctness
argument generalizes structurally, not just on the one existing test's specific commit graph. PASS.
Commit: `f0a0b8de`.

**Finding 2 — per-package glob-matcher recompile.** `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`'s
`matching_tags` compiled a fresh `globset::Glob` and rescanned the full tag list on every call, once
per package via `TagIndex::build`'s loop — even when a `[[package-set]]` rule's fixed (non-`{name}`)
`tag-template` string applies the identical template to many packages at once (measured ~640ms
wasted at 1000 packages / 41k tags in the original audit). Fixed via `select_from_tags_cached`, which
caches compile+scan results in `TagIndex::build`'s loop keyed by the template's rendered glob string.
Regression tests (`crates/callisto-graph/tests/tag_glob_cache_count_test.rs`, `#[serial]`, isolated
the same way as finding 1's counter for the same process-global-counter reason) prove 3 packages
sharing one template compile the glob exactly once (not 3 times), and 2 packages with distinct
default templates still compile separately (proving the cache keys correctly, doesn't over-collapse).
Independent review PASS. Commit: `1700f1f9`.

**Finding 3 — commit-inference pathspec bug.** `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`'s pathspecs
for commit-based severity inference were built from `pkg.manifests.iter().map(|m| m.path.clone())` —
the manifest *file* path (e.g. `crates/foo/Cargo.toml`) — instead of the package's source
*directory*, so commit-based inference only ever matched commits touching the manifest file itself,
never real source changes, making the `inference` feature (behind a Cargo feature flag) a near-total
no-op for its purpose. Fixed by reusing `crate::changed::package_paths(pkg)` — an existing,
already-tested directory-scoping helper `changed_since_last_tag` already relied on for the identical
purpose. New regression test asserts `aggregate()` hands a recording `SeverityInference` the package
directory (`crates/pkg-a`), not the manifest file path — confirmed failing against the pre-fix code.
Independent review PASS. Commit: `d3a5c434`.

**Post-PR fix — finding 3 exposed a latent bug in `location_matches`.** Real CI on PR #13
(`cargo test --all-features`, enabling the `inference` feature) caught what the scoped local
verification above missed: `changed::package_paths` emits `"."` as the pathspec for a manifest at
the workspace/package root (a single-package repo's `Cargo.toml`) — the same sentinel real git's own
pathspec engine understands as "match everything," correct for that helper's original consumer
(`changed_since_last_tag`, which shells out to real `git`). Finding 3 newly routes that `"."`
pathspec into this codebase's own hand-rolled Rust matcher instead
(`callisto-vcs`'s `commits_since_with_pathspec` → `location_matches`, using `Path::starts_with`) —
and `Path::new("Cargo.toml").starts_with(".")` is `false` in Rust, so a `"."` pathspec silently
matched **zero** commits instead of every commit: a more severe regression than finding 3 itself
fixed, specifically for single-package repos. Fixed in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`'s
`location_matches` by short-circuiting to a match whenever the pathspec itself is exactly `"."`,
mirroring real git's semantics; `ShellGit`'s shelled-out backend was never affected (delegates
matching to the real `git` binary). Regression test on a real repo confirmed failing (empty result)
before the fix. Independent review PASS (confirmed no overreach on non-`.` pathspecs, traced `"."`'s
only producer, confirmed the sibling `ShellGit` path is immune by construction). Commit: `8140b3d`.

Track 7 (`track-7-revwalk-bounding`, PR #13, not yet merged when this track was cut): `cargo nextest`

that `pinentry` can't service (no TTY to prompt on) — the test hangs ~120-140s waiting on a
gpg-agent/pinentry timeout, or fails outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". Diagnosed via
direct reproduction (confirmed NOT gpg-agent lock contention: 8 fully concurrent `git commit`s outside
nextest completed in ~1s; confirmed the specific `cargo test` vs `cargo nextest` TTY distinction is the
actual trigger) — see `feedback_diagnose_dont_guess_environment_issues.md` in the memory index for the
process this followed. Two audit agents mapped the full scope: ~66 real `git commit` call sites across
16 files build real git fixture repos without a local `commit.gpgsign=false` guard; a canonical shared
helper existed (`callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo`) but only 2 of ~14 independently-duplicated
`init_repo`/`run_git`-style helpers actually used it; a parallel audit confirmed no equivalent gap
exists for npm/pip/cargo/twine/maturin shell-outs (all go through a mockable `CommandRunner` trait in
both production and test code).

input.prompt:
Research task (read-only, no edits) in the Callisto repo at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto — a Rust-based, polyglot (Cargo/npm/PyPI) release-engineering CLI.

## Background

A downstream consumer (an agent working on a project called "michi" that uses callisto) reported this design gap:

> Lock staleness — `callisto version`'s default behavior never refreshes `Cargo.lock`, but `callisto publish` internally always runs `cargo publish --locked`. Those two of callisto's own commands are inconsistent with each other by default — nothing in status/validate/plan-publish/version warns you before it silently produces an artifact that can never successfully complete `callisto publish`. The workaround is passing `--refresh-lockfiles` (via `version_command` input in the GitHub Action), but the root cause isn't consumer-side.

I need to understand precisely whether this is real, how it manifests, and whether the same class of problem exists for npm/pnpm/yarn and PyPI (poetry/uv) too, so we can decide what to do about it (fix in callisto itself, add a diagnostic, or determine it's ecosystem-specific and doesn't generalize).

## Your task

1. **Confirm the Cargo claim precisely.**
   - Find where `callisto version` (likely `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`, function `apply_version_plan`, and its `ApplyOptions.refresh_lockfiles` field) decides whether to run `cargo update`/`uv lock`/`poetry lock` after a version bump. What is `refresh_lockfiles`'s *default* value when not explicitly set (check the CLI flag definition in `crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs` or wherever `VersionArgs`/the action's `version_command` is defined, and check `action.yml` or similar GitHub Action wiring)?
   - Find where `callisto publish` invokes `cargo publish` (likely `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`). Does it unconditionally pass `--locked`? Is this configurable, or hardcoded? What does `cargo publish --locked` actually require — i.e. under what precise condition does a stale `Cargo.lock` (relative to a `Cargo.toml` whose `version` field was just bumped, and whose internal workspace-path-dependency version requirements on siblings may also have been rewritten) cause `cargo publish --locked` to fail? Distinguish: does it fail merely because the *package's own version* changed, or because its *dependency version requirements* changed (e.g. a workspace sibling's version constraint was rewritten by callisto's cascade logic) in a way Cargo.lock's locked resolution no longer satisfies?
   - Is there any existing diagnostic, warning, or validation step anywhere in `callisto status`/`callisto validate`/`plan_publish`/`callisto version`'s own output that would surface this risk to a user before they hit the failure at actual `cargo publish --locked` time? Search broadly.

2. **Check npm/pnpm/yarn.** Does `callisto publish`'s npm path (`publish_client.rs`, look for `npm publish`, `pnpm publish`, `yarn publish`) pass any equivalent "locked"/frozen-lockfile flag? Does `npm publish`/`pnpm publish` even have a flag that would fail analogously to `cargo publish --locked` if `package-lock.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml` is stale relative to `package.json`? (You may need to reason from general npm/pnpm knowledge here since this isn't something you can execute, but ground it in what you know about how each publish command actually validates or doesn't validate against the lockfile — be precise about what you're confident of vs. inferring.) Does callisto's own npm/pnpm lockfile-refresh logic (if any exists, check `apply.rs` again) run by default or behind the same `refresh_lockfiles` flag?

3. **Check PyPI (poetry/uv/twine/python -m build).** Same question: does callisto's publish path for Python packages do anything that would fail on a stale `poetry.lock`/`uv.lock`, or is Python's publish path (typically `python -m build` + `twine upload`) fundamentally decoupled from lock-file state (since sdist/wheel builds don't consume a lock file the way `cargo publish --locked` re-resolves against `Cargo.lock`)? Ground this in what callisto's own code actually does for Python publishing.

4. **Root-cause classification.** Based on 1-3, is this staleness-causes-silent-publish-failure risk: (a) genuinely Cargo-specific, arising from `--locked`'s particular semantics and not present for npm/PyPI at all, (b) a general pattern that could theoretically bite any ecosystem but only Cargo's publish path happens to opt into strict verification today, or (c) something else? Be precise and evidence-based, not speculative.

## Output

A structured report:
- **Cargo**: confirmed mechanism (file:line for both the default `refresh_lockfiles` value and the `--locked` flag), precise failure condition, whether any diagnostic exists today.
- **npm/pnpm/yarn**: what callisto does today, whether an equivalent failure mode is even possible for these ecosystems, with your confidence level.
- **PyPI**: same.
- **Root-cause classification** per item 4, with your reasoning.
- **Where a fix would plausibly live** if we decide to build one — e.g. a new diagnostic in `plan_publish`/`callisto status` that checks "does this package's lockfile satisfy `--locked` before we'd attempt publish", or changing `refresh_lockfiles`'s default, or something else — list the realistic options you found evidence for, don't invent options unsupported by the code. Don't implement anything, just report what's there and what the realistic fix shapes are.

Keep it precise, evidence-based, file:line grounded. This is going to inform a real product/maintainer decision.

## Findings

Root cause is **ecosystem-specific in practice, general in shape**: `refresh_lockfiles` defaults to `false` for *all* ecosystems, but only Cargo's publish step (`cargo publish --locked`, hardcoded, no way to disable) turns that staleness into a hard failure — because `cargo publish` is the only one of the three that re-resolves against a lockfile as part of publishing. Confirmed by tracing what callisto's own code actually invokes:

- **npm/pnpm/yarn/bun**: none of `npm publish`/`pnpm publish`/`yarn npm publish`/`bun publish` check a lockfile at publish time at all — that's an install-time behavior (`npm ci`, `--frozen-lockfile`), not a publish-time one. Callisto's own npm publish commands don't pass any lock-verification flag.
- **PyPI**: `python -m build` + `twine upload` never touch `poetry.lock`/`uv.lock` — structurally decoupled.
- **Cargo**: `cargo publish --locked` fails the moment `Cargo.lock`'s recorded version for the bumped package doesn't match its just-written `Cargo.toml` version — which is *always* true after any bump with the default `refresh_lockfiles: false`. No diagnostic anywhere upstream (`status`/`validate`/`plan_publish`) surfaces this today.

So: **npm/pnpm/python need nothing** — there's no failure mode to guard against there, and adding a check would be inventing complexity for a problem that can't occur. This is genuinely Cargo-only.

## My stance

Given the lean-on-native-tool principle, I'd rule out flipping `refresh_lockfiles`'s default to `true` — that forces `cargo update --workspace` (which can pull in unrelated external dependency updates, not just fix the staleness) on every run for every user, whether or not they'd ever hit this. That's the opposite of minimal.

The right-sized fix: a **new diagnostic**, Cargo-only, that does one cheap, narrow check — does `Cargo.lock`'s entry for a bumped package match the version callisto just wrote to `Cargo.toml` — surfaced in `plan_publish`/`status`/`validate` output. This doesn't reimplement any of `cargo publish --locked`'s real resolution logic (that stays entirely cargo's job); it just flags the one condition callisto itself directly causes, before the user hits it downstream. Proportionate, single-ecosystem, no new behavior forced on anyone.

Worth pairing with a cheap complementary fix: when `cargo publish --locked` *does* fail with its "lock file needs to be updated" message, rewrite that error to point at `--refresh-lockfiles` — catches the rarer cascade-rewrite-triggered case the simple version-check wouldn't.

Want me to build this as a track (spec it properly given it's a real diagnostic addition, not a mechanical fix)?

content.text:
I'd land on augmenting the Action, not just documenting — pure docs don't address it proactively (michi's agent didn't find the docs before hitting the failure), and it's the lightest fix that actually closes the loop.

Concretely: change `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s default `version_command` from `"callisto version"` to `"callisto version --refresh-lockfiles"`. One line. No new Rust code, no new diagnostic, nothing added to the CLI itself — it just makes the Action's own default flow consistent with what `callisto publish`'s hardcoded `--locked` requires, which fits the lean-on-native-tool preference better than the diagnostic I floated earlier (that would've meant new `DiagnosticCode` variants, new detection logic, more surface area to review/maintain).

Trade-off worth being explicit about: `--refresh-lockfiles` runs `cargo update --workspace`, which can pull in unrelated external dependency updates alongside the version bump — not just fix the staleness. That's probably fine/expected for a release-prep step (plenty of release tools bundle lockfile refreshes into release commits), but it's a real behavior change for every Action consumer, not a no-op.

Two gaps this doesn't cover, worth a doc note regardless:
- Consumers who override `version_command` (like michi did) need to know to add the flag themselves — a README/action-docs callout on `--locked` + `--refresh-lockfiles`'s relationship covers that.
- Anyone invoking the raw CLI directly, bypassing the Action, gets no protection from an Action-level default. If that's a real enough population, the core diagnostic is still the fallback option — but I'd start with the Action fix and only add that if it turns out people are hitting this outside the Action too.

The design rationale is for packages that genuinely aren't native — it does not address a package that *looks* napi-shaped via other signals (devDependency, build script) but forgot to declare targets. That's a real, uncovered gap.

**No existing "napi-shaped" heuristic exists to detect `@napi-rs/cli`/`napi build` scripts.**

It does not read `devDependencies` or `scripts` at all.

**`callisto validate` never touches platform targets at all.**

- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs:16-159` only builds diagnostics from `.changeset/*.md` files: `EmptyChangeset`, `EmptySummary`, `UnknownPackage`, `InvalidPackageName`, `AmbiguousPackageName` (lines 68-146). It never calls into `matrix.rs`, never reads `package.json`/`pyproject.toml` for napi/maturin shape, and its `is_valid` computation (line 151-153) is purely a function of changeset diagnostics. `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/validate.rs` is a thin passthrough with no extra logic. So "validation passed despite the gap" isn't a hole in validate's napi check — validate has *no* napi/matrix check whatsoever to have a hole in.

**`DiagnosticCode` has no adjacent variant.** `crates/callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs:94-176` — the closest entries are `UnrecognisedPlatformTriple` and `DuplicatePlatformTriple`, both fired only once a triple is already declared. Nothing fires when a package looks native-shaped but declares zero triples.

**Maturin/PyPI equivalent gap: CONFIRMED, and detection infrastructure is even thinner.** `select_platform_target_source` (`matrix.rs:260-294`) applies the identical "absent → `None`, no diagnostic" logic symmetrically to `[tool.maturin].targets`. A `grep` for `build-backend`/`requires.*maturin`/`pyo3` across `callisto-graph`/`callisto-manifests` (only hits in `python.rs` test fixtures using `hatchling`/`poetry`, none for `maturin`) confirms there is no "looks maturin-shaped" heuristic anywhere — not even the loose kind `detect_npm_role` provides for napi. The maturin_pyo3_layout test in `walk.rs:1499` is about promoting a *sibling Cargo+PyPI package pair* into the graph (a different feature entirely), not about detecting undeclared maturin targets.

### Claim 2 — no reference pipeline pattern / `nativeMatrix` timing: **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED**

**`nativeMatrix` timing, precisely:** `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml:154-165`. It is computed inside the `else` branch of `if [[ "$HAS_CHANGESETS" == "true" ]]` (i.e., only on a run with *no* pending changesets) via a direct `callisto matrix --format json | jq ...` call at line 164 — this itself is standalone and doesn't depend on publish state. But it runs as line 164 of a single composite-action shell step (`callisto-orchestrate`, `action.yml:60-228`) that, if `INPUT_PUBLISH` is set, goes straight on to call `callisto publish` at line 186 in the *same* step, with no seam for a caller to inject a separate native-build matrix job in between. So the correction to the raw claim: `nativeMatrix` isn't populated "mid-way through the publish attempt" — it's populated *just before* the publish attempt starts, in the same atomic step, and is never populated at all on a run where changesets are still pending (the version-PR branch never reaches line 164). Either way, the practical problem is the same: this composite action gives no way to pause between "compute nativeMatrix" and "run publish" for a downstream matrix-build job's artifacts to land.

**`callisto matrix` CLI genuinely standalone: CONFIRMED.** `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/matrix.rs:12-27` — `handle()` just calls `load_workspace` then `callisto_graph::commands::matrix`, with a passing test on a completely empty workspace (`handle_empty_workspace_succeeds`, lines 36-53, exit code 0). `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs:16-50` confirms the graph-level `matrix()` function reads only manifests off disk via `ws.graph.packages()` — no changeset/version/publish state involved at all. `docs/00-design.md:2168-2177` states this as an explicit design invariant: "`matrix` runs independently, typically once per CI trigger before any version decision exists yet... `matrix` takes no changeset/cascade input at all."

**A reference pattern does partially exist in this repo, but it's broken/incomplete — so "not documented anywhere" is not quite right.** `ARCHITECTURE.md:472-495` shows exactly the two-job `matrix` → `build` pattern the report says is missing, using raw `callisto matrix --format json` in an early standalone job and `needs:`/`fromJSON(...)` to feed a downstream `strategy.matrix` build job — this is the "call `callisto matrix` standalone early" pattern already written down.   - The example stops at per-platform build; it never shows collecting artifacts back and calling `callisto publish` (or `callisto-action`) — the "collect artifacts → publish" half of the pipeline the report is asking about is absent even here.
  - `nativeMatrix` (the callisto-action output) isn't mentioned in this doc pattern at all — the doc example bypasses callisto-action entirely and calls raw `callisto matrix` in its own job, which is in fact the correct workaround, just never connected explicitly to callisto-action's `nativeMatrix` output or reconciled with it.

**No end-to-end example exists anywhere searched:** `grep` for `matrix`/`nativeMatrix` across `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/*.md` turns up only the partial/broken pattern above and prose design rationale — no working matrix→build→collect→publish workflow YAML. `nativeMatrix` itself is referenced only in `action.yml` and internal `.claude/` planning artifacts, never in README/ARCHITECTURE/docs.

**Callisto doesn't dogfood this at all.** The repo has no `package.json`/`pyproject.toml` anywhere (pure Rust workspace), and its own `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:69-76` calls `callisto-action` with `publish: "true"` directly in a single job — no matrix/build job, no consumption of `nativeMatrix` output whatsoever. So there's no self-example to point to either.

**Fix shapes:**
- This is **primarily a docs/example gap**, not a required code change: the underlying pieces (`callisto matrix` standalone, `fromJSON(needs.job.outputs.x)` matrix wiring) already work as shown by `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s own partial example and the CLI's demonstrated independence from publish state. A corrected, complete example workflow — call `callisto matrix` in an early job, fan out a real build job (using `callisto build`/existing napi/maturin build tooling instead of the fictional `publish-target`), upload artifacts, then a final job that downloads artifacts and calls `callisto-action`/`callisto publish` — would close most of the gap without touching Rust code.

That's a minor but genuine action-level correctness bug worth fixing alongside any doc update.
- Whether to also thread `nativeMatrix` computation into a separable, always-populated action step (independent of the changesets/publish branch) is a legitimate design choice for whoever owns the action, but is not required to unblock consumers — "run raw `callisto matrix` standalone, early, in your own job" is already fully supported by the code today and just needs to be written down as the sanctioned pattern, replacing the broken `publish-target`-based example currently in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**Fix shapes:**
- This is **primarily a docs/example gap**, not a required code change: the underlying pieces (`callisto matrix` standalone, `fromJSON(needs.job.outputs.x)` matrix wiring) already work as shown by `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s own partial example and the CLI's demonstrated independence from publish state. **Out of scope for this repo:** the claim that lumen/monokl/prism sibling repos also lack this pattern cannot be verified from within the callisto repository — no references to those repos exist here.</result>

## Findings

**Claim 1 — CONFIRMED, and worse than reported.** `callisto matrix` returning `{}` for undeclared napi/maturin packages is *documented as intentional* (`docs/00-design.md:2135-2140`) for genuinely-non-native packages — but there's no signal distinguishing that from "forgot to declare targets." More importantly: `callisto validate` doesn't have a hole in its napi check — **it has no napi/maturin/platform-target check at all**, for either ecosystem. It only ever looks at changeset files. And the "reuse existing napi-shape detection" idea I'd have assumed exists doesn't — `detect_npm_role` in `walk.rs` checks something unrelated (platform-stub packages via `os`/`cpu` fields), never `devDependencies` or `scripts`. This would be genuinely new detection logic on both sides (napi: check `devDependencies["@napi-rs/cli"]`/`scripts` for `napi build`; maturin: check `build-system.requires`/`build-backend` for `maturin` in `pyproject.toml`) — maturin's detection infrastructure is even thinner than napi's.

**Claim 2 — PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, one real bug found along the way.** The timing claim needed a correction: `nativeMatrix` isn't populated "mid-way through publish" — it's computed in the same atomic action step, right before publish starts, but it's **only reached when there are no pending changesets**; on a version-PR run, that line never executes. Actual bug: `action.yml` documents `nativeMatrix`'s default as `"Empty array"`, but it's actually left completely unset in that branch — any consumer doing `fromJSON(steps.x.outputs.nativeMatrix)` would hit a JSON parse error, not get `[]`. That's a real, small action-level bug, independent of the docs question.

On the reference-pattern gap: `ARCHITECTURE.md` already has a partial example, but it's broken — it calls `callisto publish-target`, a subcommand that **doesn't exist in the CLI** (the doc itself flags this as unimplemented), and it stops at "build," never showing the collect-artifacts-then-publish half. No working end-to-end example exists anywhere, and callisto doesn't dogfood this itself (pure Rust workspace, no napi/maturin packages of its own).

## Recommendation

Two separable pieces of work:

1. **Real code change** (Claim 1): new `DiagnosticCode` variant(s) for "package looks native-shaped but declares no targets," new detection logic for both ecosystems, plus a design decision on whether `validate` re-derives this itself or merges `matrix`'s diagnostics (they're currently fully decoupled). This has enough real scope and design surface to warrant going through the actual spec/plan pipeline, not a mechanical fix.
2. **Docs + one small action fix** (Claim 2): fix `nativeMatrix`'s unset-vs-`"[]"` bug in `action.yml` (quick, mechanical), and replace `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s broken example with a correct, complete matrix→build→collect→publish workflow.

Want me to start with #2 (cheap, self-contained) while we decide whether #1 becomes a full track?

6	    required: false

8	    description: 'Custom version command to run (defaults to "callisto version")'
9	    required: false

12	    description: 'Commit message for the Version PR'
13	    required: false
14	    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
15	  title:
16	    description: 'Title for the Version PR'
17	    required: false
18	    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
19	  pr_label:
20	    description: 'Label to attach to the Version Packages Pull Request'
21	    required: false
22	    default: 'callisto: release'
23	  create_github_release:
24	    description: 'Whether to create GitHub Release entries for calculated tags'
25	    required: false
26	    default: 'true'
27	  setup_git_user:
28	    description: 'Whether to automatically configure git user.name and user.email'
29	    required: false
30	    default: 'true'
31	  branch:
32	    description: 'Base branch for Version PRs'
33	    required: false
34	    default: 'main'
35	  cwd:
36	    description: 'Working directory path if workspace is in a subfolder'
37	    required: false
38	    default: '.'
39	
40	outputs:
41	  hasChangesets:
42	    description: 'Whether pending changesets were found'
43	    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.hasChangesets }}
44	  published:
45	    description: 'Whether packages were published'
46	    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.published }}
47	  publishedPackages:
48	    description: 'JSON list of published packages'
49	    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.publishedPackages }}
50	  nativeMatrix:
51	    description: 'JSON array of native platform build targets discovered from manifests (callisto matrix output). Empty array when no native packages are present or callisto matrix is not yet available.'
52	    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.nativeMatrix }}
53	
54	runs:
55	  using: 'composite'
56	  steps:
57	    - name: Setup Callisto Environment
58	      uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
59	
60	    - name: Orchestrate Version PR or Publish
61	      id: callisto-orchestrate
62	      shell: bash
63	      env:
64	        INPUT_PUBLISH: ${{ inputs.publish }}
65	        INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.version_command }}
66	        INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE: ${{ inputs.commit_message }}
67	        INPUT_TITLE: ${{ inputs.title }}
68	        INPUT_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.pr_label }}
69	        INPUT_CREATE_GITHUB_RELEASE: ${{ inputs.create_github_release }}
70	        INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER: ${{ inputs.setup_git_user }}
71	        INPUT_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.branch }}
72	        INPUT_CWD: ${{ inputs.cwd }}
73	        GH_TOKEN: ${{ env.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
74	        NPM_TOKEN: ${{ env.NPM_TOKEN }}
75	        CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ env.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
76	        TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ env.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
77	        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
78	        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
79	      run: |
80	        set -e
81	        if [[ "$INPUT_CWD" != "." ]]; then
82	          cd "$INPUT_CWD"
83	        fi
84	
85	        echo "::group::1. Inspecting Workspace Status"
86	        set +e
87	        callisto status --check
88	        STATUS_EXIT=$?
89	        set -e
90	        if [[ $STATUS_EXIT -eq 1 ]]; then
91	          HAS_CHANGESETS=true
92	        elif [[ $STATUS_EXIT -eq 2 ]]; then
93	          HAS_CHANGESETS=false
94	        else
95	          echo "::error::callisto status --check exited with unexpected code $STATUS_EXIT (expected 1 for pending changesets or 2 for none pending)"
96	          exit 1
97	        fi
98	        echo "::endgroup::"
99	
100	        if [[ "$HAS_CHANGESETS" == "true" ]]; then
101	          echo "hasChangesets=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
102	          echo "published=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
103	
104	          EXISTING_PR_BODY=$(gh pr list --head callisto/version-packages --json body --jq '.[0].body // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
105	
106	          echo "::group::2. Composing Version PR Body"
107	          if [[ -n "$EXISTING_PR_BODY" ]]; then
108	            PR_BODY=$(echo "$EXISTING_PR_BODY" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
109	          else
110	            PR_BODY=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
111	          fi
112	          echo "$PR_BODY"
113	          echo "::endgroup::"
114	
115	          echo "::group::3. Bumping Package Versions ($INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND)"
116	          read -ra _version_cmd <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
117	          "${_version_cmd[@]}"
118	          echo "::endgroup::"
119	
120	          echo "::group::4. Creating / Updating Version Packages Pull Request"
121	          if [[ -n $(git status --porcelain) ]]; then
122	            if [[ "$INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER" == "true" ]]; then
123	              git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
124	              git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
125	            fi
126	
127	            git checkout -B callisto/version-packages
128	            git add -A
129	            git commit -m "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE"
130	            git push origin callisto/version-packages --force
131	
132	            if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
133	              gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color "0e8a16" --description "Release packages" 2>/dev/null || true
134	            fi
135	
136	            EXISTING_PR=$(gh pr list --head callisto/version-packages --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
137	            if [[ -n "$EXISTING_PR" ]]; then
138	              gh pr edit "$EXISTING_PR" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" || true
139	              if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
140	                gh pr edit "$EXISTING_PR" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" || true
141	              fi
142	            else
143	              if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
144	                gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" || gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH"
145	              else
146	                gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH"
147	              fi
148	            fi
149	
150	            echo "### Version Packages PR Created/Updated" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
151	            echo "$PR_BODY" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
152	          fi
153	          echo "::endgroup::"
154	        else
155	          echo "hasChangesets=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
156	
157	          # Emit native matrix targets for downstream build jobs, deduplicated
158	          # by artifactName in case the same triple is declared by more than
159	          # one package's platform-target group. set -o pipefail ensures a
160	          # hard `callisto matrix` error (e.g. malformed manifest, conflicting
161	          # platform-target sources) fails this step instead of silently
162	          # producing empty output.
163	          set -o pipefail
164	          NATIVE_MATRIX=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)') || { echo "::error::callisto matrix failed"; exit 1; }
165	          echo "nativeMatrix=$NATIVE_MATRIX" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
166	
167	          if [[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]; then
168	            echo "::group::2. Calculating Topological Publish Plan"
169	            PLAN_JSON=$(callisto plan-publish --format json)
170	            echo "$PLAN_JSON"
171	            echo "::endgroup::"
172	
173	            # Wire NPM_TOKEN into npm config so npm publish can authenticate.
174	            # NPM_TOKEN is forwarded explicitly in this step's env: block so it
175	            # is available regardless of how the caller sets it.
176	            if [[ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]]; then
177	              npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken "$NPM_TOKEN"
178	            fi
179	
180	            echo "::group::3. Executing Package Publishing"
181	            if [[ "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "true" ]]; then
182	              echo "Executing custom publish script: $INPUT_PUBLISH"
183	              read -ra _publish_cmd <<< "$INPUT_PUBLISH"
184	              "${_publish_cmd[@]}"
185	            else
186	              callisto publish
187	            fi
188	            echo "::endgroup::"
189	
190	            echo "published=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
191	            echo "publishedPackages<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
192	            echo "$PLAN_JSON" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
193	            echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
194	
195	            echo "::group::4. Tagging Release Commits & Updating Major Version Pointer Aliases"
196	            callisto tag --plan "$PLAN_JSON" --floating-major || true
197	            git push origin --tags || true
198	            echo "::endgroup::"
199	
200	            if [[ "$INPUT_CREATE_GITHUB_RELEASE" == "true" ]]; then
201	              echo "::group::5. Creating GitHub Release Entries"
202	              while IFS= read -r ENTRY; do
203	                [[ -z "$ENTRY" ]] && continue
204	                TAG=$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.tagName')
205	
206	                if ! echo "$ENTRY" | jq -e 'has("isPrerelease") and (.isPrerelease|type=="boolean")' > /dev/null; then
207	                  echo "::error::release entry for tag $TAG has a missing or non-boolean isPrerelease field"
208	                  exit 1
209	                fi
210	
211	                echo "Creating GitHub Release for tag: $TAG"
212	
213	                EXTRA_FLAGS=""
214	                if [[ "$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.isPrerelease')" == "true" ]]; then
215	                  EXTRA_FLAGS="--prerelease"
216	                fi
217	
218	                gh release create "$TAG" --title "$TAG" --generate-notes $EXTRA_FLAGS || true
219	              done < <(echo "$PLAN_JSON" | jq -c '.releases[]?')
220	              echo "::endgroup::"
221	            fi
222	
223	            echo "### Packages Published Successfully" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
224	          else
225	            echo "published=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
226	            echo "No changesets pending and no publish command provided."
227	          fi
228	        fi

  create_github_release:
    description: 'Whether to create GitHub Release entries for calculated tags'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  setup_git_user:
    description: 'Whether to automatically configure git user.name and user.email'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  branch:
    description: 'Base branch for Version PRs'
    required: false
    default: 'main'
  cwd:
    description: 'Working directory path if workspace is in a subfolder'
    required: false
    default: '.'

outputs:
  hasChangesets:
    description: 'Whether pending changesets were found'
    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.hasChangesets }}
  published:
    description: 'Whether packages were published'
    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.published }}
  publishedPackages:
    description: 'JSON list of published packages'
    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.publishedPackages }}
  nativeMatrix:
    description: 'JSON array of native platform build targets discovered from manifests (callisto matrix output). Empty array when no native packages are present or callisto matrix is not yet available.'
    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.nativeMatrix }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Setup Callisto Environment
      uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto

    - name: Orchestrate Version PR or Publish
      id: callisto-orchestrate
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_PUBLISH: ${{ inputs.publish }}
        INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.version_command }}
        INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE: ${{ inputs.commit_message }}
        INPUT_TITLE: ${{ inputs.title }}
        INPUT_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.pr_label }}
        INPUT_CREATE_GITHUB_RELEASE: ${{ inputs.create_github_release }}
        INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER: ${{ inputs.setup_git_user }}
        INPUT_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.branch }}
        INPUT_CWD: ${{ inputs.cwd }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ env.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        NPM_TOKEN: ${{ env.NPM_TOKEN }}
        CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ env.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ env.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        set -e
        if [[ "$INPUT_CWD" != "." ]]; then
          cd "$INPUT_CWD"
        fi

        echo "::group::1. Inspecting Workspace Status"
        set +e
        callisto status --check
        STATUS_EXIT=$?
        set -e
        if [[ $STATUS_EXIT -eq 1 ]]; then
          HAS_CHANGESETS=true
        elif [[ $STATUS_EXIT -eq 2 ]]; then
          HAS_CHANGESETS=false
        else
          echo "::error::callisto status --check exited with unexpected code $STATUS_EXIT (expected 1 for pending changesets or 2 for none pending)"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "::endgroup::"

        if [[ "$HAS_CHANGESETS" == "true" ]]; then
          echo "hasChangesets=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "published=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          EXISTING_PR_BODY=$(gh pr list --head callisto/version-packages --json body --jq '.[0].body // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)

          echo "::group::2. Composing Version PR Body"
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING_PR_BODY" ]]; then
            PR_BODY=$(echo "$EXISTING_PR_BODY" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
          else
            PR_BODY=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
          fi
          echo "$PR_BODY"
          echo "::endgroup::"

          echo "::group::3. Bumping Package Versions ($INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND)"
          read -ra _version_cmd <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
          "${_version_cmd[@]}"
          echo "::endgroup::"

          echo "::group::4. Creating / Updating Version Packages Pull Request"
          if [[ -n $(git status --porcelain) ]]; then
            if [[ "$INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER" == "true" ]]; then
              git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
              git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
            fi

            git checkout -B callisto/version-packages
            git add -A
            git commit -m "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE"
            git push origin callisto/version-packages --force

            if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
              gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color "0e8a16" --description "Release packages" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi

            EXISTING_PR=$(gh pr list --head callisto/version-packages --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
            if [[ -n "$EXISTING_PR" ]]; then
              gh pr edit "$EXISTING_PR" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" || true
              if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
                gh pr edit "$EXISTING_PR" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" || true
              fi
            else
              if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
                gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" || gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH"
              else
                gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH"
              fi
            fi

            echo "### Version Packages PR Created/Updated" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "$PR_BODY" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi
          echo "::endgroup::"
        else
          echo "hasChangesets=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Emit native matrix targets for downstream build jobs, deduplicated
          # by artifactName in case the same triple is declared by more than
          # one package's platform-target group. set -o pipefail ensures a
          # hard `callisto matrix` error (e.g. malformed manifest, conflicting
          # platform-target sources) fails this step instead of silently
          # producing empty output.
          set -o pipefail
          NATIVE_MATRIX=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)') || { echo "::error::callisto matrix failed"; exit 1; }
          echo "nativeMatrix=$NATIVE_MATRIX" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          if [[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]; then
            echo "::group::2. Calculating Topological Publish Plan"
            PLAN_JSON=$(callisto plan-publish --format json)
            echo "$PLAN_JSON"
            echo "::endgroup::"

            # Wire NPM_TOKEN into npm config so npm publish can authenticate.
            # NPM_TOKEN is forwarded explicitly in this step's env: block so it
            # is available regardless of how the caller sets it.
            if [[ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]]; then
              npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken "$NPM_TOKEN"
            fi

            echo "::group::3. Executing Package Publishing"
            if [[ "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "true" ]]; then
              echo "Executing custom publish script: $INPUT_PUBLISH"
              read -ra _publish_cmd <<< "$INPUT_PUBLISH"
              "${_publish_cmd[@]}"
            else
              callisto publish
            fi
            echo "::endgroup::"

            echo "published=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "publishedPackages<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "$PLAN_JSON" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            echo "::group::4. Tagging Release Commits & Updating Major Version Pointer Aliases"
            callisto tag --plan "$PLAN_JSON" --floating-major || true
            git push origin --tags || true
            echo "::endgroup::"

            if [[ "$INPUT_CREATE_GITHUB_RELEASE" == "true" ]]; then
              echo "::group::5. Creating GitHub Release Entries"
              while IFS= read -r ENTRY; do
                [[ -z "$ENTRY" ]] && continue
                TAG=$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.tagName')

                if ! echo "$ENTRY" | jq -e 'has("isPrerelease") and (.isPrerelease|type=="boolean")' > /dev/null; then
                  echo "::error::release entry for tag $TAG has a missing or non-boolean isPrerelease field"
                  exit 1
                fi

                echo "Creating GitHub Release for tag: $TAG"

                EXTRA_FLAGS=""
                if [[ "$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.isPrerelease')" == "true" ]]; then
                  EXTRA_FLAGS="--prerelease"
                fi

                gh release create "$TAG" --title "$TAG" --generate-notes $EXTRA_FLAGS || true
              done < <(echo "$PLAN_JSON" | jq -c '.releases[]?')
              echo "::endgroup::"
            fi

            echo "### Packages Published Successfully" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          else
            echo "published=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "No changesets pending and no publish command provided."
          fi
        fi

1. **Package Discovery Guard**: Verifies all workspace crates and packages are accounted for in `callisto.toml`.
2. **Schema & Config Health**: Validates `callisto.toml` fields and types.
3. **Changeset Syntax Integrity**: Verifies `.changeset/*.md` frontmatter and package IDs.
4. **Pre-Flight Release Simulation**: Simulates `callisto plan-publish` topological DAG sorting to ensure zero cyclic dependencies before PR merge.

### Ultra-Fast Local Git Hooks (`pre-commit` & `pre-push`)

Callisto standardizes local developer hook workflows in [`justfile`](justfile):
- `just pre-commit` (~100ms): Fast formatting check before local commits.
- `just pre-push` (~1.5s): Formatting check and Clippy lints before remote pushes.
- `just hooks`: Installs native `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and `.git/hooks/pre-push` shell scripts in one command.

---

## 11. Engineering Invariants & Quality Controls

All contributions to Callisto must adhere to the following 4 engineering invariants:

1. **Safe Rust Strictness**: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is enforced across all 10 workspace crates.
2. **Zero Clippy Warnings**: Code must compile with zero warnings under `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
3. **Format Enforcement**: Code formatting must strictly match `cargo fmt --check`.
4. **Comprehensive Test Suite Coverage**: Unit, integration, doctests, and lifecycle E2E tests must pass (`just ci`).

---

## 12. Zero-Config Multi-Platform Native Matrix Auto-Discovery (`callisto matrix`) [partially implemented]

> **Status: napi-rs and maturin platform-target discovery, plus npm/PyPI runtime-version constraints, are implemented** (`callisto matrix [--package <name>]`, `--format text|json` via the global flag). Java (JNI) target discovery, .NET native-AOT target discovery, and the `callisto publish-target` subcommand described later in this section remain unimplemented and are planned for a future release.

To eliminate configuration duplication and configuration drift across native Rust, NAPI-RS, Maturin (Python), and Java (JNI) polyglot monorepos, `callisto matrix` provides dynamic matrix auto-discovery:

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               CALLISTO NATIVE MATRIX AUTO-DISCOVERY                     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Workspace Manifests (Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml)        │
│ ↳ Single Source of Truth: napi.targets, maturin.targets, engines.node  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ callisto matrix --format json                                          │
│ ↳ Dynamically computes runner OS, target triples, & runtime versions   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ GitHub Actions / GitLab CI Job Matrix                                  │
│ ↳ Parallel native build matrix execution without hardcoded YAML arrays  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Manifest-Driven Target Auto-Detection

1. **NAPI-RS (`package.json`)**: Auto-detects `napi.targets` (e.g. `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) and maps them to a GitHub Actions runner label per triple (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`/`macos-13`, `windows-latest`, plus `cross`-gated Linux/Android/FreeBSD targets).
2. **Maturin (`pyproject.toml`)**: Auto-detects `tool.maturin.targets` and Python runtime compatibility bounds.
3. **Runtime Engine Compatibility**: Automatically extracts Node.js (`engines.node`) and Python (`requires-python`) version ranges directly from package manifests, eliminating duplicate version strings in CI YAML. Java (`java.version`/`pom.xml`) extraction is not yet implemented, consistent with this section's status note above.

### Zero-Config GitHub Actions Workflow Pattern

```yaml
jobs:
  matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.discover.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
      - id: discover
        run: echo "matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build:
    needs: matrix
    strategy:
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.matrix.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
      - run: callisto publish-target --package ${{ matrix.package }} --target ${{ matrix.target }}
```

---

## 13. Hermetic Build Systems & Custom Orchestration (Bazel, Buck2, Nix, GitLab CI)

**3. `docs/00-design.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` — the actual spec/design docs**

I need a precise, evidence-based answer, not speculation.

## What I need you to establish

1. **napi-rs's own standard release convention** (ground this in what you know about napi-rs's official project template / `@napi-rs/cli` conventions, be explicit about what's general napi-rs knowledge vs. what you found in this repo's code): typically a napi-rs project publishes N platform-specific npm packages (e.g. `my-pkg-linux-x64-gnu`, `my-pkg-darwin-arm64`), each containing just the built `.node` binary plus a minimal `package.json` with `os`/`cpu` fields, and one main package with `optionalDependencies` pointing at all of them. 2. **The actual missing link**: after a matrix-driven per-platform CI job builds a `.node` binary (via `napi build --platform --release` or similar, run by the consumer's own workflow, NOT by callisto), does ANYTHING in callisto help place that binary into the correct platform-stub package's directory before `callisto publish` runs? Search for any code that copies, moves, or stages a build artifact into a package directory (grep for things like "artifact", "stage", "copy" in `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs` and `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs` and `crates/callisto-cli/src/`). Is this staging step something callisto's `matrix` output gives you enough information to do easily yourself (e.g. does `artifactName`/the platform-stub package's manifest path tell a consumer exactly where the binary needs to land), or is it a real, nontrivial gap requiring custom glue?

3. **What existing consumers actually do**: this repo's own `.github/actions/callisto-action` — does it, or any doc/example in this repo, show or reference the actual binary-placement step at all, even informally? If genuinely nothing addresses this anywhere in the repo, say so plainly.

4. **Severity/scope judgment**: given 1-3, classify the binary-placement gap as: (a) a real, load-bearing gap that makes the current matrix feature incomplete for its stated purpose (auto-discovery alone doesn't get you to a working publish without significant custom glue), (b) a gap but a shallow/well-understood one (the `artifactName` + platform-stub manifest path already give you everything you need, it's just not documented), or (c) not really callisto's job at all (napi-rs's own tooling, e.g. `napi build`'s own `--platform` flag or `napi artifacts`/`napi prepublish` commands, already handles this and callisto correctly stays out of it — note if you're confident napi-rs's own CLI has commands for this).

Direct, evidence-based answers to each of the 5 points above, file:line grounded where the claim is about this repo's code, explicitly flagged as "general napi-rs knowledge, not verified against this repo" where it isn't.
