spec_file_path: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/specs/SPEC-002-native-artifact-placement.json
criterion_id: AC-001

Run in correction mode: revise the affected criterion (and any dependent fields/criteria) and return the full corrected spec@1 with revision_note set.

Contradiction report (from the maintainer, backed by verified research, not just a preference):

The implementation was just changed AGAIN, after this spec's prior AC-001 correction already shipped and was gated. The maintainer questioned whether `{package_name}-{triple}` (the format the currently-committed spec describes) was itself the right convention, since it embeds the full Rust target triple including its vendor component (e.g. "aarch64-apple-darwin"). Research was done using WebSearch/WebFetch against real sources before implementing:

- napi-rs's own official docs (https://napi.rs/docs/deep-dive/release) state published platform packages are named `<name>-<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]`, e.g. `@scope/addon-darwin-arm64`, `@scope/addon-win32-x64-msvc`, `@scope/addon-linux-x64-gnu` -- never the raw Rust target triple, never a vendor component ("apple"/"pc"/"unknown"). The same docs explicitly recommend using this SAME platform-arch-abi suffix for CI artifact names as for the published package name, and napi-rs's own `napi artifacts` CLI tool expects downloaded artifacts to already carry a `binaryName.platform-arch-abi` suffix when repackaging them -- a real interop reason, not just cosmetics.
- By contrast, Rust CLI binaries distributed via cargo-dist/GitHub Release (a different, out-of-scope distribution model -- SPEC-002's own non_goals already exclude this as "Tier 2") DO use the full raw triple with vendor component -- confirmed via real ripgrep GitHub releases, e.g. `ripgrep-15.2.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`. That convention does not apply here because SPEC-002 covers only the napi/maturin native-library artifact-placement path, not CLI binary distribution.

Given SPEC-002 is specifically about the napi/maturin path, the maintainer decided the napi-rs convention is the correct one to follow, not the cargo-dist one.

What the system actually does now (verified by reading the committed code directly, commit 87682d5 on branch track-9-matrix-artifact-placement in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto):

- `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs` no longer has `artifact_name_for_package_triple(package_name: &str, triple: &str) -> String`. It now has:
  ```rust
  pub(crate) fn artifact_name_for_package_platform(
      package_name: &str,
      platform: &str,
      arch: &str,
      abi: Option<&str>,
  ) -> String {
      match abi {
          Some(abi) => format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}-{abi}"),
          None => format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}"),
      }
  }
  ```
- `build_platform_target` calls it with the already-destructured `platform`/`arch`/`abi` values from `triple_to_role(triple)` (the same values that populate `PlatformTarget.platform`/`.arch`/`.abi`), not the triple string.
- Real examples now produced: `native-mod-darwin-arm64` (package "native-mod", aarch64-apple-darwin -> platform "darwin", arch "arm64", abi None), `other-pkg-linux-x64-musl` (platform "linux", arch "x64", abi Some("musl")).
- This is collision-safe for the same reason as before: every triple in `triple_host_runner_use_cross`'s 18-triple table maps to a distinct (platform, arch, abi) tuple, so uniqueness is preserved; combined with package_name (already workspace-unique), artifactName stays globally unique per workspace.

What needs correcting in the spec (read the full spec first to confirm exact current wording before editing -- do not assume my summary of field names is complete):
1. `scope`'s Rust-change description currently describes `artifact_name_for_package_triple(package_name: &str, triple: &str) -> String` returning `format!("native-{package_name}-{triple}")` -- this is now doubly stale (both the old "native-" prefix AND the triple-based approach were already superseded). Rewrite to describe `artifact_name_for_package_platform(package_name: &str, platform: &str, arch: &str, abi: Option<&str>) -> String` and its platform-arch-abi format, citing the napi-rs convention as the reason.
2. `api_surface`'s entry for the renamed function needs the same signature/description update.
3. `AC-001`'s criterion text needs to assert the new format and function name/signature, with concrete examples (e.g. via a two-package-same-triple scenario, but now asserting `<packageName>-<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]` shaped values, not triple-shaped ones).
4. The non_goal about "Preserving the exact literal string format `native-{triple}`... as a stable, versioned contract" (if still present with that exact old wording) needs to be checked for staleness -- it may need rewording since the format identity has changed again, or it may already generalize fine; read it and decide.
5. Check whether any other criterion (e.g. AC-002, which also implicitly depends on artifactName's shape for the dedup test) needs a matching wording adjustment -- read all criteria and decide, don't assume none do.

Ground every claim in the actual current file contents (spec and code) as you go, the same way the prior correction round did. This is the spec's second correction pass this session; treat it with the same rigor as the first (auditor + exit-gate re-review before returning).

Contradiction report (from the maintainer, backed by verified research, not just a preference):

The implementation was just changed AGAIN, after this spec's prior AC-001 correction already shipped and was gated. The maintainer questioned whether `{package_name}-{triple}` (the format the currently-committed spec describes) was itself the right convention, since it embeds the full Rust target triple including its vendor component (e.g. "aarch64-apple-darwin"). Research was done using WebSearch/WebFetch against real sources before implementing:

- napi-rs's own official docs (https://napi.rs/docs/deep-dive/release) state published platform packages are named `<name>-<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]`, e.g. `@scope/addon-darwin-arm64`, `@scope/addon-win32-x64-msvc`, `@scope/addon-linux-x64-gnu` -- never the raw Rust target triple, never a vendor component ("apple"/"pc"/"unknown"). The same docs explicitly recommend using this SAME platform-arch-abi suffix for CI artifact names as for the published package name, and napi-rs's own `napi artifacts` CLI tool expects downloaded artifacts to already carry a `binaryName.platform-arch-abi` suffix when repackaging them -- a real interop reason, not just cosmetics.
- By contrast, Rust CLI binaries distributed via cargo-dist/GitHub Release (a different, out-of-scope distribution model -- SPEC-002's own non_goals already exclude this as "Tier 2") DO use the full raw triple with vendor component -- confirmed via real ripgrep GitHub releases, e.g. `ripgrep-15.2.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`. That convention does not apply here because SPEC-002 covers only the napi/maturin native-library artifact-placement path, not CLI binary distribution.

Given SPEC-002 is specifically about the napi/maturin path, the maintainer decided the napi-rs convention is the correct one to follow, not the cargo-dist one.

What the system actually does now (verified by reading the committed code directly, commit 87682d5 on branch track-9-matrix-artifact-placement in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto):

  ```rust
  pub(crate) fn artifact_name_for_package_platform(
      package_name: &str,
      platform: &str,
      arch: &str,
      abi: Option<&str>,
  ) -> String {
      match abi {
          Some(abi) => format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}-{abi}"),
          None => format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}"),
      }
  }
  ```

3. `AC-001`'s criterion text needs to assert the new format and function name/signature, with concrete examples (e.g. via a two-package-same-triple scenario, but now asserting `<packageName>-<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]` shaped values, not triple-shaped ones).
4. The non_goal about "Preserving the exact literal string format `native-{triple}`... as a stable, versioned contract" (if still present with that exact old wording) needs to be checked for staleness -- it may need rewording since the format identity has changed again, or it may already generalize fine; read it and decide.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression test proving the native artifact placement loop lives INSIDE
# the INPUT_PUBLISH guard (SPEC-002 AC-003's "not merely somewhere after
# NATIVE_MATRIX computation" clause, and AC-004's second sentence).
#
# test_native_artifact_placement.sh extracts the loop body in isolation
# (between its own ::group::/::endgroup:: markers), so it would keep
# passing even if the loop were moved outside the guard entirely. This
# test instead extracts from the guard's own `if` line through the loop's
# ::endgroup:: -- inclusive of the guard condition itself -- so it fails
# if the loop is ever hoisted above (or the guard condition weakened
# around) that `if` line.
set -u
ACTION_YML="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/action.yml"

# The range starts at the guard's exact `if` line and ends at the FIRST
# ::endgroup:: after it -- which, if the loop is still correctly placed
# immediately inside the guard, is the loop's own closing marker. A
# missing/moved guard or loop means this range no longer captures both
# together, and the appended `fi` below then either closes nothing
# (syntax error) or closes a guard with an empty body (no gh calls even
# when INPUT_PUBLISH=true).
extract_guarded_snippet() {
  sed -n '/if \[\[ -n "\$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "\$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" \]\]; then/,/::endgroup::/p' "$ACTION_YML"
  echo "fi"
}

run_case() {
  local native_matrix="$1"
  local input_publish="$2"
  local calls_file tmp_script workdir
  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
  workdir="$(mktemp -d)"
  tmp_script="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "gh() { echo \"\$*\" >> '${calls_file}'; return 0; }"
    echo "mkdir() { command mkdir \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "cd '${workdir}'"
    echo "NATIVE_MATRIX=$(printf '%q' "$native_matrix")"
    echo "GITHUB_RUN_ID=999"
    echo "INPUT_PUBLISH=$(printf '%q' "$input_publish")"
    extract_guarded_snippet
  } > "$tmp_script"
  bash "$tmp_script"
  local code=$?
  cat "$calls_file"
  rm -f "$tmp_script" "$calls_file"
  rm -rf "$workdir"
  return $code
}

fail=0
MATRIX='[{"artifactName":"pkg-a-darwin-arm64","packageDir":"packages/pkg-a"}]'

# Positive control: INPUT_PUBLISH=true must reach the loop and call gh.
out=$(run_case "$MATRIX" "true"); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ "$out" != *"run download 999 --name pkg-a-darwin-arm64"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL positive control (INPUT_PUBLISH=true must place artifacts): code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS positive control (INPUT_PUBLISH=true places artifacts)"
fi

# AC-003/AC-004: INPUT_PUBLISH unset -> the guard must skip the loop
# entirely. If the loop were ever hoisted above this guard's `if` line,
# this case would start calling gh and fail.
out=$(run_case "$MATRIX" ""); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ -n "$out" ]]; then
  echo "FAIL AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH unset must skip placement): code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH unset skips placement)"
fi

# INPUT_PUBLISH="false" -> same guard, same expectation.
out=$(run_case "$MATRIX" "false"); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ -n "$out" ]]; then
  echo "FAIL AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH=false must skip placement): code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH=false skips placement)"
fi

exit $fail

## 9. GitHub Actions Orchestration (`callisto-action`)

Callisto includes a built-in composite action ([`.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`](.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml)) for CI/CD automation and supports 3 release paradigms (see [`docs/release-paradigms.md`](docs/release-paradigms.md)):

```mermaid
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%%
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runner as GitHub Actions Runner
    participant Verify as Job 1: verify (Mandatory CI Gate)
    participant Action as Job 2: release (needs: [verify])
    participant CLI as callisto CLI
    participant GH as GitHub API (gh CLI)

    Runner->>Verify: push / workflow_dispatch
    Verify->>Verify: format · lint · test · WASM check · cargo-deny audit
    alt CI Fails
        Verify-->>Runner: Exit 1 — Job 2 cancelled
    else CI Passes
        Verify->>Action: Trigger release job
        Action->>CLI: callisto status --check
        alt Pending Changesets
            Action->>CLI: callisto version
            Action->>CLI: callisto compose-pr-body
            Action->>GH: Create or update callisto/version-packages PR
        else Version PR Merged (zero changesets)
            Action->>CLI: callisto plan-publish --format json
            Action->>CLI: callisto publish
            Action->>CLI: callisto tag --floating-major
            Action->>GH: Create GitHub Releases & update floating major alias (v1)
        end
    end
```

### Complete Action Input Matrix

| Input | Default | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `publish` | `""` | Command to execute when publishing packages (`cargo publish`, `pnpm publish`, `moon run :publish`). |
| `version_command` | `"callisto version"` | Custom versioning command. |
| `commit_message` | `"chore(release): version packages"` | Commit message for the Version Packages PR. |
| `title` | `"chore(release): version packages"` | Pull Request title. |
| `pr_label` | `"callisto: release"` | Label automatically attached to the Version Packages PR. |
| `create_github_release` | `"true"` | Toggle GitHub Release entry creation for calculated tags. |
| `setup_git_user` | `"true"` | Automatically configure `git config user.name` & `user.email` bot credentials. |
| `branch` | `"main"` | Base branch for Version PRs. |
| `cwd` | `"."` | Working directory path if workspace root is nested in a subfolder. |

### Diagnostic Problem Matchers & Toolchain Isolation

- **Inline PR Annotations**: Registered [`.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json`](.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json) in `setup-callisto`. Automatically highlights invalid `.changeset/*.md` syntax or missing package IDs as inline callouts on PR diff lines.
- **Pre-installed Toolchain Targets**: All toolchain setup steps declare `targets: wasm32-wasip1` up-front alongside `rustfmt` and `clippy`. This prevents parallel `rustup` download race conditions when Moon executes 10 crate tasks in parallel.
- **Unbuffered Stream Output & UI Accordions**: Long-running shell commands use `::group::` and `::endgroup::` annotations for foldable UI accordions, streaming stdout and stderr live to the runner console.

---

input.new_string:
### Lockfile Staleness (`--refresh-lockfiles`)

`callisto version` bumps manifest versions (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`) but
does not regenerate lockfiles by default. `callisto publish` always runs `cargo publish
--locked`, which fails if `Cargo.lock` is stale relative to the bumped `Cargo.toml` versions --
this can happen when bumping an interdependent Cargo package changes what a workspace member's
own `Cargo.lock` entry should say.

`callisto version --refresh-lockfiles` closes this gap for Cargo and Python: it runs `cargo
update --workspace` (Cargo) and, if present, `uv lock` or `poetry lock --no-update` (Python)
after bumping, before staging changes for commit (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`). It is
opt-in (default `false`) since most workspaces don't need it -- override the action's
`version_command` input to `"callisto version --refresh-lockfiles"` if your workspace has
interdependent Cargo or Python packages whose versions are bumped together.

npm-family lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lockb`) are not
refreshed by `--refresh-lockfiles`: unlike `cargo publish --locked`, neither `npm publish` nor
`pnpm publish` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`) pass any lockfile-
strictness flag, so a stale npm-family lockfile does not fail publish the way a stale
`Cargo.lock` does. This has not been a reported problem for npm/pnpm; if that changes, add the
equivalent `npm install --package-lock-only` / `pnpm install --lockfile-only` step to
`--refresh-lockfiles`'s existing Cargo/PyPI implementation rather than a separate workaround in
the Action.

tables: `napi.rs`'s `triple_to_role` (platform/arch/abi — shared with §G.4.5's unrelated napi

`artifactName` is always `"native-" + triple`. A triple absent from *either* table is excluded
from `targets[]` and reported as an `UnrecognisedPlatformTriple` diagnostic naming the triple and
the package — never a hard error, since one unrecognised triple in a declaration must not hide
the ones that were recognised. A triple repeated within one package's own declaration is
likewise not an error: the duplicate is dropped (first occurrence wins) and reported as
`DuplicatePlatformTriple`, since a hand-maintained `napi.targets` array is exactly the kind of
list a copy-paste duplicates without anyone noticing, and two identical `PlatformTarget` entries
would mean two identical CI jobs racing on the same artifact upload.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about invalid character restrictions for the `actions/upload-artifact` action:

## Invalid Characters for Artifact Names

The following characters are not allowed in artifact names: Double quote ", Colon :, Less than <, Greater than >, Vertical bar |, Asterisk *, Question mark ?, Carriage return \r, Line feed \n, Backslash \, Forward slash /

## Why These Restrictions Exist

These characters are not allowed in the artifact name due to limitations with certain file systems such as NTFS. To maintain file system agnostic behavior, these characters are intentionally not allowed to prevent potential problems with downloads on different file systems.

The forward slash (/) is particularly problematic because it's a path separator in many file systems, which is why users who try to use branch names with slashes (like `feature/text-annotation`) encounter errors when uploading artifacts with those names included.

spec_file_path: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/specs/SPEC-002-native-artifact-placement.json
criterion_id: AC-001

Run in correction mode: revise the affected criterion (and any dependent fields) and return the full corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. Write the corrected spec to disk when it passes canon:auditor and canon:exit-gate, same as your prior two correction passes on this spec this session.

Contradiction report (a real defect found by the maintainer's own review, not a preference):

The spec (and the code, until just now) described `artifactName` as `{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}[-{abi}]` with `package_name` embedded verbatim. This is a real bug for npm scoped packages: a `PackageId`'s name can legitimately be e.g. `@scope/addon` (npm scope syntax), and `actions/upload-artifact` rejects `/` in artifact names (confirmed via GitHub's own upload-artifact issue tracker: forbidden characters are `" : < > | * ? \r \n \ /`). Embedding `@scope/addon` verbatim would produce `artifactName: "@scope/addon-darwin-arm64"`, which fails every `actions/upload-artifact`/`gh run download` call for that package -- the exact class of defect this spec exists to prevent (AC-001's whole purpose is making artifactName safe for that pipeline).

What the system actually does now (verified by reading the committed code, commit a8db2b1 on branch track-9-matrix-artifact-placement in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto):

`crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs`'s `artifact_name_for_package_platform` now sanitizes `package_name` first:
```rust
pub(crate) fn artifact_name_for_package_platform(
    package_name: &str,
    platform: &str,
    arch: &str,
    abi: Option<&str>,
) -> String {
    let package_name = package_name.replace('/', "-");
    match abi {
        Some(abi) => format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}-{abi}"),
        None => format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}"),
    }
}
```
So `@scope/addon` on `darwin`/`arm64` (no abi) now produces `artifactName: "@scope-addon-darwin-arm64"` -- no `/`.
